papers.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
authors: C. J. L. de la Rosa
papers.summary: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. The extracted activation barriers reach values substantially exceeding room-temperature thermal energies, indicating that disorder-driven conduction onset remains relevant well beyond cryogenic transport.

papers.title: The Weight Is in the Reading: Hidden States in Memristors, Memlumors, and Electrochemical Transistors
papers.summary: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. Building on Chua's formulation of memristive systems, we separate the state variable, which evolves with the excitation history, from the observation map that converts it into a measured signal, and we define the weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol. Three platforms show the consequences: a memristor, in which the same voltage writes and reads; a memlumor, in which light both modifies the state and produces the photoluminescence that reports it; and an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT), in which the gate writes and the channel reads. In the transistor, two states prepared by different histories give the same channel current at a specific drain bias and become distinguishable again when the bias is changed, while the stored charge persists and the gate current continues to separate them. Published experiments provide precedents: a drain-bias-dependent cancellation of the OECT transient, and trapped charges in perovskite memlumors that are invisible to conventional time-resolved photoluminescence but revealed by a read-write-read sequence. A synaptic weight is therefore not a property of the material alone but of the material together with its readout, and reports of synaptic behavior should specify what is stored, what is measured, and how one is inferred from the other.

papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
papers.summary: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidity for one day. These results demonstrate that mica substrates enable high-mobility, flex-out-compatible In2O3-based TFTs.

papers.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
papers.summary: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
papers.summary: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. Numerical renormalization group calculations across the full coupling parameter space show that the resonance is embedded in a broad region of elevated switching ratio at intermediate hybridization $Γ\approx Δ$, while both weaker and stronger coupling reduce it to a thin isolated line. Finite temperature smooths the underlying singlet-doublet transition and lowers the supercurrent amplitude, but affects the open and closed states comparably and leaves the switching ratio largely intact. Within a zero-bandwidth two-level model, a second dot level is shown to open a leakage channel that grows as the two levels approach in energy. Raising the output barrier and the realistic presence of inter-level Coulomb repulsion, however, suppress the leakage.

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
papers.summary: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

papers.title: An opto-electrically decoupled phototransistor for solar-blind ultraviolet detection
papers.summary: Solar-blind ultraviolet (UV) photodetectors have been primarily developed using ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors, where the wide bandgap enables low dark current and intrinsic solar-blind selectivity. However, the same wide-bandgap nature limits carrier modulation, particularly doping control and junction engineering, imposing fundamental challenges for high-sensitivity detection and scalable integration. Here, we demonstrate an opto-electrically decoupled solar-blind UV phototransistor by integrating a perovskite p–n photovoltage generator with a carbon nanotube (CNT) field-effect transistor. This architecture separates photon conversion from carrier transport, where the perovskite heterojunction generates a photovoltage that electrostatically modulates the CNT channel without interfacial carrier transfer. Under 265 nm illumination, the device achieves a responsivity of 2908 A W−1, a specific detectivity of 1.6 × 1013 Jones, and rise/decay times of 5.6/15.5 ms. The low-temperature fabrication process is compatible with silicon back-end-of-line integration, providing a route toward highly integrated solar-blind UV sensing with front-end bandpass filtering, beyond conventional UWBG semiconductor systems.

papers.title: Impact of a process-induced interfacial layer on ferroelectric switching and reliability in AlScN/ β -Ga2O3 MFS capacitors
papers.summary: In this study, we demonstrate AlScN-based metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor capacitors directly integrated on a heteroepitaxial β-Ga2O3. Structural analysis reveals the presence of a process-induced amorphous intermixed layer at the AlScN/β-Ga2O3 interface. The fabricated devices exhibit ferroelectric switching behavior, characterized by counterclockwise hysteretic current–voltage loops with an on/off current ratio of >102, which is limited by the intermixed interfacial layer. Piezo-response force microscopy measurements confirm the intrinsic polarization switching capability through phase reversal and butterfly-shaped amplitude loops. Furthermore, positive-up-negative-down measurements indicate polarization switching while revealing a switching current asymmetry. We identify that this asymmetry originates from the internal electric field and charge trapping associated with the interfacial defect layer. This interfacial instability primarily affects the device performance observed during retention (103 s) and endurance (5 × 103 cycles) tests, suggesting significance of the interface toward stable ferroelectric operation in AlScN/β-Ga2O3 devices.
